disposition: The reported zero-initialization source is overwritten before these key uses, or is erased state that is fenced from further key use; not a hard-coded operational key finding.

sinks.evidence: JournalKey::signing_owner_key fills all 32 bytes using HKDF expand; failure propagates before AEAD construction (durable.rs:243-251).
Same signing-owner HKDF key path as sink 1; decryption uses the returned initialized key.
messages::step expands 64 bytes, then key() copies exact 32-byte halves; send calls step before constructing the cipher (messages.rs:186-225).
Receive uses a key from the same step or a previously stored skipped message key. The zeroed exhausted receive chain is fenced by receive_limit before further stepping (traffic.rs:448-537).
The test attacker calls the real step on the deliberately disclosed chain before each forged frame; the input is not a zero initializer (tests.rs:1604-1623).
The isolated key-only replacement test fills fresh with getrandom before copying it to the chain and deriving the message key (tests.rs:1686-1703). This does not endorse that candidate transition.

JournalKey::provision fills its complete allocation through getrandom; read_file fills it through read_exact before returning. Both errors propagate; sink receives that private JournalKey field (durable.rs:264-280,323-342).
Same JournalKey owner/read path as sink 7, used to decrypt the authenticated journal image.

Initial MAC key comes from SharedSecret::derive_key/export_for_protocol; later bootstrap confirmations come from schedule/derive. Both fill the complete HKDF output; export copies all bytes. The independent vector test also derives from explicit synthetic IKM (bootstrap.rs:811-827,884-907,959-966,1935-1965; sdk/purpose.rs:64-92).

Verification uses the same initial_key/schedule-derived confirmation objects; ResponderState::Prepared holds the derived initiator confirmation. Closed/Idle or removed confirmation fails first (bootstrap.rs:641-661,873-874,1026-1028).
Direct HKDF expansion overwrites the entire derived buffer and propagates failure before HMAC (cancellation.rs:341-349).
Direct archive-domain HKDF expansion overwrites derived and propagates failure before HMAC (closure/archive.rs:10-19).

begin_session_closure fills the report key with getrandom before report_mac. Reopen decodes exact key bytes with key(); the zero placeholder paired with absent report returns None (closure.rs:70-84,315-324).

begin_fanout_cleanup fills all key bytes with getrandom before report_mac, persists that same key, and reopening decodes the stored key for Abandoning. Reserved/terminal placeholders do not become that key (fanout/abandonment.rs:280-305; fanout/codec.rs:155-173).

The adversarial test opens the actual journal key then calls write_intent_key, whose complete HKDF output is used to MAC the deliberately changed body (anchoring/tests.rs:2023-2027; durable.rs:233-241).
Direct root-derived confirmation HKDF overwrites secret with error propagation before HMAC (rekey/completion.rs:448-456).
Direct responder-confirmation HKDF overwrites secret with error propagation before HMAC (rekey/response.rs:147-156).

begin_closed_epoch_resolution fills report_key using getrandom before setting Some and computing the ID; decoding copies exact stored bytes. Absent or erased key returns State, not a zero-key MAC (resolution.rs:216-218,316-320; traffic.rs:182-186).
The test explicitly expands the root into the entire mac_key with expect before computing its forged confirmation (tests/send_budget.rs:561-568). Test location alone is not the disposition.
Direct retired-report HKDF overwrites derived and propagates failure before HMAC (retired_report.rs:332-341).
The test expands the recovered root into the entire confirmation buffer before verifying the actual peer tag (tests.rs:1964-1975).
Direct terminal-receipt HKDF overwrites derived and propagates failure before HMAC (write_intent/retired_cleanup/erasure.rs:40-49).
write_intent_key fills the complete derived output before authenticator receives it; failure propagates (durable.rs:233-241; write_intent.rs:334-337).

limitations: Manual source/data-flow review, not a fresh runtime test or proof of the whole protocol.
Counts apply only to the original 780-result analysis; indices cannot be transferred to newer SARIF files.
Explicit host-supplied/stored key bytes and deliberately disclosed test keys are separate from an unfilled allocation.
No claim of universal key quality, entropy health, KDF/AEAD security, nonce uniqueness, or physical erasure.
